page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.3xlarge is a compute-focused cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and deployed on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Hardware specifications include 12.0 GB of total system memory, resulting in a strict 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor is equipped with 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and FMA. This instance contains no local SSD storage and no integrated GPU accelerators, relying on network storage with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight average multi-core processing efficiency paired with lower single-core speeds. The ecs.ic5.3xlarge instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 5055.0, a stress-ng multi-core benchmark score of 8838.44, and a PassMark CPU score of 10093.16. Single-core performance is lower, with Geekbench single-core reaching 995.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1105.38. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 57.8 GB/sec for reads and 40.23 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests reveal strong multi-threaded utility, such as 43.18 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 8.63 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Conversely, single-threaded gzip compression performs in the bottom 10% (19.27 GB/sec), and medium-sized LLM prompt processing is constrained at 14.46 tokens per second.

The 1:1 ratio of vCPUs to RAM offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallel compute tasks that require low memory overhead per execution thread. The trade-off is a constrained memory footprint, which prevents deployment of large in-memory databases or memory-heavy applications. The instance is suited for multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight API infrastructure.

Utilizing x86_64 architecture on KVM, it features 35 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 vector extensions, and a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. Its hardware configuration maintains a low memory allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Performance benchmarks display solid multi-core execution, achieving 5055.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 8838.44 in stress-ng multi-core, and 8.63 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, though single-threaded performance is weaker. This profile provides clear cost efficiency for thread-heavy workloads with limited memory requirements, such as software compilation, static web serving, and parallelized data batch processing.
